corpusOverrides.note: Both started from Ja and both came out clean. 畀 dropped from two flagged strokes (max 98°) to none over 18° because the simplified file writes the two bars of 田 in the dictionary order. 歃 dropped from five flagged strokes (max 99°, a five-stroke permutation) to none over 22° because MM writes the 臼 halves in the dictionary order. selection.json records both starting corpora and reasons.

directionProbe.threshold: angle over 60° between dictionary and candidate start-to-end vectors
directionProbe.note: 畀 and 歃 disappeared when the corpus changed. The remaining four (茀, 鬢, 豳, 蘋) were all resolved by reordering. The endpoint assignment check added 紕, 轡, 繽, 紓 and 紲, whose 糸 strokes run in the same direction and differ only in order. Recomputed against the published order and paths, no stroke is over 60°.

subThresholdSlants.method: direction-probe rows recomputed against the published order and paths: 9 rows between 45° and 60°, none corrected
subThresholdSlants.note: Short opening dots and left dots the dictionary draws vertically or steeper than the licensed corpora (庳 1 at 56°, 紕 5 at 47°, 轡 18 at 53°, 痹 1 at 57°, 繽 7 at 54°, 擯 4 at 50°, 鬢 16 at 53°, 裼 1 at 53°, 愃 4 at 55°). Kept as licensed geometry, as in the earlier batches.

sourceTransform.note: Two dictionary groups carry a horizontal offset, translate(12, -830), after 厲 in batch 4 and three glyphs in batch 5. serve.py, source-checks.mjs and direction-probe.mjs accept translate(x, -y), and the published paths come from the licensed corpus, so the offset only affects what the review sheet draws.
